articles.title: Arjun Prasad turns promise into IGPL title, Ganapathy finishes runner-up
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Arjun Prasad did not have to wait long for his first Indian Golf Premier League title.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Arjun Prasad did not have to wait long for his first Indian Golf Premier League title. Just his second appearance on the IGPL and his first in India was enough for the young professional to turn promise into a trophy at the \ IGPL Invitational 2026 presented at Qutab Golf Course in New Delhi.Prasad, representing Unico Gurugram Tuskers GC, who won the team event, produced the round of the tournament when it mattered most, firing a brilliant seven-under 63 in the third round to finish at 16-under 194. The effort gave him a four-shot cushion over another of the league's emerging young stars, Veer Ganapathy, who was representing the Bengaluru Stallions and finished runner-up at 12-under 198.The victory was built on three rounds of controlled golf—66, 65, and 63—but it was the manner in which Prasad handled the final stretch that underlined his composure. He turned in 31 and came home in 32, making seven birdies without dropping a shot. A run of three consecutive birdies on the front nine, followed by two more on the back nine and birdies at the 17th and 18th, allowed him to pull away from a field packed with established names."Competition is pretty high over here as well. We have some outstanding players who have done phenomenally well internationally," Prasad said after his victory. "I just kept it very simple from the very first day, just kept on following the process, and I'm grateful that I was able to do it all three days and get on top.""The course is playing very differently from what we are generally used to. The fairways are softer, and the greens were soft as well, but the rough was extremely high, and the greens were slower, so it was tough to judge that. Hitting the ball on the fairway and then getting it onto the green was very important. If you missed the green, then those up-and-downs were very tough to make,” Prasad said.Prasad's charge also came at the expense of an intriguing battle involving Ganapathy, who had shared the lead after the second round and was among the players expected to challenge for the title. The Bengaluru youngster carded a 63 of his own in the third round and finished at 12-under 198, four shots behind Prasad.For Ganapathy, the week was another reminder of his growing presence on the IGPL stage. After rounds of 68 and 67, he produced his best golf when the pressure was highest, attacking from the outset and giving himself a chance to stay in the title race."The course is, of course, amazing and in good condition. I mean, it's scoring, but at the same time you have to keep the ball in play, which is important," Ganapathy said. "I think the first two days I struggled a bit, but then I came back well, and I finished well. Today from the start, it was like I was just trying to go as low as I could, and a few putts fell, a few good shots, and yeah, it was a good week."Prasad, who had made his IGPL debut in Ras Al Khaimah in the United Arab Emirates only a couple of weeks earlier, acknowledged that Ganapathy's presence near the top added another layer to the final-round challenge."I'm so happy for the young guy. He played so well," Prasad said. "I had the opportunity to play with him on day one as well, and he's an extremely gritty young kid who has a lot of potential. Having him move up the leaderboard was a great motivation for me to do my best and improve.”Experience also played a role in Prasad's victory. He said a series of top-10 finishes and near misses over the previous season had helped him understand how to handle the critical moments better."Last year I had a lot of top-10 finishes, and I came close. I could only close it one time," he said. "The way I was talking to myself in the round and the kind of headspace I was in, I think that's a lot of experience in it as well. All those things last year and even this year have come together for this thing."Behind the leading duo, RVR Delhi Blue Bulls captain Shiv Kapur finished third at 11-under 199 after a final-round 65. Four-time IGPL winner Gaganjeet Bhullar carded a five-under final round to finish fourth at 10-under 200, while Olympian Udayan Mane, Karandeep Kochhar, and Harshjeet Sethie shared fifth place.The tournament had a strong women's presence too, with Kashika Misra finishing as the leading woman golfer. After taking the lead with rounds of 66 and 64, Misra carded a six-over 76 on the final day and finished tied 20th. Her performance over the first two rounds, however, had put her firmly at the center of the tournament narrative.Ganapathy was among those impressed by the young golfer. "She's played incredible golf the whole week. She was literally destroying us, I would say," he said. "All respect to her. It's not that easy, and coming out here and beating all the men is tough. Props to her."The mixed field was one of the aspects Ganapathy felt made the IGPL different from conventional golf tournaments.The team competition added another dimension. Unico Gurugram Tuskers, powered by Prasad's title-winning performance, finished on 23-under to claim team honours. Shat Mishra, Tushar Pannu, and Shaurya Binu completed the winning combination, with the Tuskers finishing four shots ahead of Vimtra Chennai Lions GC, who were second at 19-under. Gaganjeet Bhullar's fourth-place finish and Harshjeet Sethie's tied-fifth effort led the Lions' challenge.Five teams, Bengaluru Stallions, Flying Man Kolkata, Auro Goa Eagles, RVR Delhi Blue Bulls, and Punjab Raptors shared third place at 18-under.For Ganapathy, the team element has become an important part of the league's appeal."IGPL introducing the team format is something new, and I think it's a great thing because now it becomes like a camaraderie between the four players," he said. "Keeping our placements aside, we have a really good bond on and off the course."Prasad echoed that sentiment after helping the Tuskers secure the team title."This week I was playing for the Gurugram Tuskers, and I think the camaraderie is something I'm getting the hang of. It's new, and it's exciting," he said.At Qutab, however, it was Prasad who had the final word. His 63 transformed a close contest into a decisive victory and gave the IGPL another new champion in an increasingly competitive season.For a player who arrived in the league only weeks ago, the breakthrough could hardly have been louder: three rounds, 16-under par and a trophy to show for it.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Alfred Dunhill Links Championship: Matthew Jordan moves into contention with Casey Jarvis leading by one
articles.summary: Matthew Jordan survives 'sledging' from outspoken television presenter Piers Morgan to move into contention at Alfred Dunhill Links; South African Casey Jarvis leads by one on 11 under after a 67 at Kingsbarns
articles.body:
The Royal Liverpool member is looking for his first DP World Tour win in his 183rd tournament and he shrugged off the good-natured criticism from the television presenter - his amateur playing partner for the team part of the event - to card six birdies and an eagle at Carnoustie.

His one mishap was a bogey at the ninth, his final hole, but he got to 10 under and into a four-way tie for second place.

"Yeah, with Piers, the amount of sledging that goes on towards me is incredible," said Jordan.

"We are supposed to be a team but honestly it's all about him and that's how he makes it.

"I think Peter Jones (star of Dragons Den) missed a two-foot putt on 15 and he (Morgan) comes up to me - because I hit it to two foot as well - and he says: 'Don't do a Jonesy'.

"So that kind of puts the heebie-jeebies in you over that small putt. He just cuts at me like that and every time I seem to do something good, it's him taking the limelight."

South African Casey Jarvis leads by one on 11 under after a 67 at Kingsbarns but the round of the delay belonged to Spaniard Rocco Repetto Taylor who had an eight-under 64 at Kingsbarns, the second of three courses being used for the first three rounds with St Andrews also hosting on the final day.

The 23-year-old had four birdies and an eagle in his final nine holes to sit 10 under alongside Jordan and South African MJ Daffue.

Defending champion Bob MacIntyre is at eight under after a 65 at Kingsbarns, where Brooks Koepka shot a 67 to sit level with the Scot.

Tommy Fleetwood is at six under after a four-under 68 at Kingsbarns, as is Ryder Cup team-mate Matt Fitzpatrick with a 70 at the same course.

In their first DP World Tour appearances in nearly four years, Lee Westwood got to four under after a 69 at Kingsbarns but fellow LIV golfer Ian Poulter went out in 41 at Carnoustie on his way to 76 which left him four over.

Watch the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship played over the Old Course at St Andrews, Carnoustie Golf Links and Kingsbarn Golf Links on Sky Sports Golf this Friday from midday.

articles.title: Sustainable construction, effective pollution control need of the hour, says MahaMetro MD Hardikar
articles.summary: MahaMetro MD Shravan Hardikar urges sustainable construction and stricter dust control at GRIHA Regional Conclave 2026 in Pune; MoUs signed with colleges.
articles.body: Pune: Sustainable and environment-friendly construction practices are essential to address the environmental impact of rapid urbanisation, Maharashtra Metro Rail Corporation managing director Shravan Hardikar said at the inauguration of GRIHA Regional Conclave 2026 in Pune on Wednesday.Speaking at the event, organised by GRIHA (Green Rating for Integrated Habitat Assessment) Council, which is jointly established by Ministry of New & Renewable Energy (MNRE) and The Energy and Resources Institute (TERI), and Sustainability Initiative (SI), Hardikar said effective implementation of environmental regulations, regular monitoring and adoption of sustainable construction practices were necessary to control pollution from the construction sector.“If sustainable development is to be achieved, everyone needs to take the initiative. Those who do not adopt environment-friendly construction practices should face punitive action. With construction activity increasing across cities, dust pollution is also rising, making effective implementation of dust-control measures essential,” Hardikar said.The conclave, held at Hotel Conrad in Koregaon Park, was themed ‘Pathways for a Low Carbon Future: Building to Infrastructure’. It brought together architects, developers, infrastructure experts, govt officials, academics and sustainability professionals to discuss low-carbon buildings, resilient infrastructure, climate finance and sustainable urban development.A key highlight of the inaugural session was the signing of two MoUs. GRIHA signed an MoU with Vishwakarma University, Pune, with GRIHA CEO Sanjay Seth and Dr Priti Dhanwat, Dean, School of Architecture and Planning, Vishwakarma University, exchanging the agreement. A second MoU was signed with Dr D. Y. Patil College of Architecture, Mumbai, and was exchanged by Shabnam Bassi, Director, Sustainable Buildings Division, TERI, and Prof Dinesh Zope.Prof Sunil S. Bhagwat, Director, IISER Pune, said India could potentially take a leadership role globally in sustainability in the coming years. “Sustainability is important, but economics and human needs are equally significant. There is a need for extensive research and innovative initiatives to achieve environment-friendly and sustainable development,” he said.Sanjay Seth said Pune is a rapidly growing city, and it needs infrastructure to support its rapid growth, but such development should not come at the cost of the environment. “All stakeholders need to work together to promote sustainable and environment-friendly construction. The conclave can provide direction for such collaborative efforts,” he said.The event began with a fireside chat with environmental experts Dr Prasad Modak and Ar. Anagha Paranjape-Purohit. Projects and schools that had received GRIHA ratings were also felicitated. A GRIHA delegation also visited Saarthi, a green building in Pune, as part of the programme.The plenary session on ‘Scaling Sustainability: From Green Buildings to Resilient Cities and Infrastructure’ examined ways to reduce energy, carbon, water and resource consumption through sustainable building practices. Another roundtable session, on ‘Moving Towards Low Carbon Transition: Business Strategy, Climate Finance and Building Stakeholder Capacity to Derive Carbon Value’, discussed green finance, business strategies, carbon markets and the economic potential of verified emission reductions.The conclave was attended by GRIHA CEO Sanjay Seth, TERI’s Shabnam Bassi, IISER Pune Director Prof Sunil Bhagwat, Dr Prasad Modak, VK Group Chairman & Managing Director Hrishikesh Kulkarni, former PMRDA chief engineer Vivek Kharwadkar, Developer Sarvesh Javadekar, Architect Anuja Pandit, Sustainability Initiative trustee Ar. Anagha Paranjape-Purohit, Upendra Deshpande, Vijay Sane, Prof. Dinesh Zope and Dr Priti Dhanwat, among others. articles.title: Ravens Announce Lamar Jackson News Ahead of Week 4 Titans Game
articles.summary: The Baltimore Ravens have made final rulings on several players for their Week 4 showdown with the Tennessee Titans.It was already announced by Ravens head c...
articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens have made final rulings on several players for their Week 4 showdown with the Tennessee Titans.

It was already announced by Ravens head coach Jesse Minter that edge rusher Trey Hendrickson was going to be out after getting a procedure done on his finger. That left other questions about the roster going into the game.

Baltimore released its last injury report before the Titans game. It answered some big questions, including the status of quarterback Lamar Jackson after he dealt with a back injury that limited him earlier in the week.

Baltimore Ravens Reveal Lamar Jackson's Status for the Titans Game

After some health concerns, Jackson is officially good to go with his back injury, as he did not have an injury designation. His fellow offensive players, Zay Flowers (hamstring) and Ronnie Stanley (toe), were listed as questionable.

Last season, Jackson missed at least one practice a week, but only because he was playing hurt. This suggests he is officially good to play and will be on the field barring any major setbacks before kickoff.

This season, Jackson has thrown for 745 yards and 4 touchdowns to 1 interception . He's added another 124 yards and 1 touchdown on the ground.

Lamar Jackson Officially Good to Go for Ravens vs. Titans

This is a massive relief for Ravens fans to see that Jackson is good to go. Last year, he missed multiple games with all kinds of injuries. That really set the franchise back; losing him again is something they don't want to repeat in 2026.

The real question is whether Jackson will have his top receiver, Flowers, and his top offensive lineman, Stanley, on the field. Those two are critical to the team's success if the Ravens want to win.

Losing Hendrickson is already a big blow, but the team has at least some depth at edge rusher. Tavius Robinson will be the top pass rusher, with Mike Green and rookie Zion Young getting more reps on the field.

Stanley might be the more important player to get back on the field with the offensive line issues. Both Ravens centers have been ruled out, putting rookie first-round pick Vega Ioane in line for his first career start at center.

The winless Titans should be a winnable game for the Ravens, but injuries could hold them back. It's a good thing that Jackson is available, as he will be the key to a Baltimore win. If he can help carry this offense and get the running game going with Derrick Henry, this should be a 3-1 start for them.

articles.title: Tom Kim gains exemption from South Korea’s military service after securing Asian Games gold medal
articles.summary: Tom Kim claimed a three-shot victory in the Men's Individual Strokeplay event to secure gold at the Asian Games and exempt him from completing full mandatory military service; watch Kim in action throughout the PGA Tour season, live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
The 24-year-old took a one-shot lead heading into the final round, but carded a sensational six-under 64 to secure gold and finish three shots clear of Japan's Higa Kazuki, China's Wenyi Ding and Sadom Kaewkanjana of Thailand.

Kim top-scored for the International Team at last week's Presidents Cup against Team USA before making an immediate trip to Japan, where he was among three South Korean male golfers to feature at Kasugai Country Club.

South Korean men must enlist in the military by the age of 28, serving for 18-21 months, but an Asian Games gold medal or Olympic medal provides an exemption from full military service.

The four-time PGA Tour winner, who won the Genesis Scottish Open in July, needed to win either the individual or team event to secure that exemption and, effectively, avoid having to pause his golfing career.

A gold medal means Kim will now be able to undergo basic military training, which lasts less than a month, similar to former Tottenham captain Heung-Min Son, who completed a three-week basic military training camp in 2020 after he led South Korea to gold at the Asian Games in 2018.

"It's unbelievable," Kim said. "I had one goal, and to be able to represent Korea and to win the gold medal, it's something that I will never forget in my career."

Kim partnered with Seonghyeon Kim and Doyeob Mun for the team event. The South Korean trio entered the final round one shot clear at the top of the leaderboard, but would finish two shots behind China in second.

Kim got off to an excellent start during Saturday's final round, going four under on his front nine, with birdies on holes two, four, six and eight.

He added another on the 11th, before extending his lead to 19 under with an eagle on the 13th hole.

A bogey on the 17th set him back to 18 under, but Kim would make par on the last to secure his spot at the top of the podium.

His compatriot Mun placed tied for eighth at eight under par, while fellow South Korean, Seonghyeon Kim, tied-24th at one over par.

Kim previously tried to secure his exemption at the 2024 Paris Olympics, where he finished four shots outside the bronze-medal position. The 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles would have been his last opportunity before the age limit.

Sungjae Im and Si Woo Kim took team gold in the 2023 Asian Games, earning their military exemptions, although Sangmoon Bae - part of the 2015 Presidents Cup team - is among the golfers to have seen their career disrupted by military service .

articles.title: 'I like being the first to do things': Meet Pranavi Urs, who made history with Asian Games golf gold
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Pranavi Urs made history at the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya on Saturday, becoming the first Indian woman golfer to win an individual gold medal
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Pranavi Urs made history at the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya on Saturday, becoming the first Indian woman golfer to win an individual gold medal at the Games.The 23-year-old from Mysuru held her nerve in a tense final round to finish one stroke ahead of the field. Her victory also helped India win the women's team silver medal.Pranavi finished the four-day competition at 15-under 265, with a final-round score of even-par 70.Triple bogey, then a strong comebackPranavi began the final round with a three-stroke lead but saw her advantage disappear after a triple bogey on the third hole. She responded strongly, making three birdies on the sixth, 10th and 13th holes to get back in control. She then held on to her one-stroke lead to complete a historic victory.China's Yin Ruoning won silver after shooting 67 in the final round. She finished at 14-under 266.Singapore's Shannon Tan also ended at 266 after a 68. She won the bronze medal following a playoff.'The first will always be the first'Pranavi was delighted after completing the biggest victory of her career."I like being the first to do things," a jubilant Pranavi said after the historic triumph."People will come along to do more but the first will always be the first," she said.Her victory ended a long wait for India in Asian Games golf.Pranavi's gold was India's first golfing gold since Shiv Kapur won the men's individual title in 2002. It was also India's best performance in golf since the 1982 Delhi Asian Games, when golf became part of the Games programme.Lakshman Singh won the men's individual gold that year. He was also part of India's gold-winning team alongside Amit Luthra and Rajiv Mohta.Pranavi helps India win team silverPranavi's individual gold was followed by a team silver for India.The Indian women's team consisted of Pranavi, Aditi Ashok and Diksha Dagar. The two best scores from the three golfers were counted for the team competition.India finished with a combined score of 14-under 546, behind gold medallists China, who finished at 22-under 538.Aditi produced her best round of the week, shooting 67. She made five consecutive birdies but also had a double bogey and a bogey. She finished tied 14th in the individual event at 2-over 282.Diksha shot 77 in the final round and finished tied 23rd with a total of 12-over.The result gave India its best-ever performance in the women's team golf event at the Asian Games.Who is Pranavi Urs?Pranavi Sharath Urs was born on April 15, 2003, in Mysuru, Karnataka. She started playing golf as a child after watching her father and brother play at the Jayachamaraja Wadiyar Golf Club in Mysuru.She made her mark in junior golf, winning the 2018 Singha World Junior Championship in Thailand and the All India Junior Girls Championship.Pranavi turned professional in 2020 and competed on the domestic women's professional golf circuit before moving to the international stage.She represented India at the Hangzhou Asian Games in 2023, finishing 13th in the individual event and fourth in the team event.From domestic golf to the international stagePranavi has competed on the Ladies European Tour (LET) and produced several notable results. She finished third at the Andalucía Costa del Sol Open de España in 2024 and tied for third at the Dormy Open Helsingborg that year. She also finished fourth at the Hero Women's Indian Open 2025 and tied for fifth at the Lacoste Ladies Open de France 2025.In 2025, she won the IGPL Invitational Mumbai, becoming the first Indian woman to win a professional open-field tournament featuring male golfers.She finished 17th in the 2024 Ladies European Tour standings during her first full season on the tour.Pranavi was also conferred the Arjuna Award in 2023 for her achievements and contribution to Indian golf.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Asian Games 2026: Golfer Tom Kim wins gold to secure military service exemption
articles.summary: Golfer Tom Kim wins gold at the Asian Games to secure an exemption from mandatory service in South Korea's military.
articles.body:
18 T Kim (Kor); -15 K Higa (Jpn), W Ding (Chi), S Kaewkanjana (Tha); -11 W-H Wang (Tpe)

Tom Kim won gold at the Asian Games to secure an exemption from mandatory service in South Korea's military.

The 24-year-old led going into the final round and produced a brilliant six-under-par 64 to finish 18 under and claim victory by three strokes.

There were signs of nerves with a bogey on the 17th but, after five birdies and an eagle prior to that, Kim had the margin for error and tapped in for par on the last before letting out a roar, his relief clear to see.

Able-bodied South Korean males are usually required to undertake between 18 and 21 months of military service before the age of 28.

However, the government rewards Asian Games champions and Olympic medal-winners of any colour with a service exemption bar basic training, which lasts less than a month.

Athletes who have previously secured the exemption include former Tottenham footballer Son Heung-min, who served for only three weeks in 2020 having won the Asian Games with his country two years earlier.

Kim rushed from the Presidents Cup in the United States to tee off at the Kasugai Country Club in Japan, having to manage on just six hours of sleep and a 14-hour time difference.

His efforts were worth it as the world number 32 can now continue his career, in which he has already won four PGA Tour titles and triumphed at the Scottish Open in July, with minimal disruption.

Kim had previously come close to securing an exemption at the Paris Olympics in 2024, finishing day one tied for third before ultimately finishing eighth.

However, his compatriot SH Kim, 28, missed out on a military exemption as South Korea could only win silver in the team event, alongside Tom Kim and Mun Do-yeob, who has already completed his service.

articles.title: Tom Kim se libra de la mili tras ganar el oro en los Juegos Asiáticos
articles.standfirst: Su apresurada salida de la Presidents Cup le ha salido rentable al ganar el torneo de golf de la competición asiática que le permite quedar exento del servicio militar surcoreano
articles.summary: Su apresurada salida de la Presidents Cup le ha salido rentable al ganar el torneo de golf de la competición asiática que le permite quedar exento del servicio militar surcoreano
articles.body: el surcoreano Tom Kim se marchó a toda prisa de la Presidents Cup sin esperar a ver si finalmente Japón se imponía a Estados Unidos. Había acabado su partido individual, el segundo de la jornada dominical, y firmado el cuarto punto que daba a su equipo. La celeridad por abandonar Medinah (Chicago) se debía a su participación en los Juegos Asiáticos. El torneo de golf arrancaba tres días después en el Kasugai Country Club (Kasugai, prefectura de Aichi, Japón). Y ganar el oro tenía un premio de lo más atractivo: librarse del servicio militar obligatorio. Kim se hubiera perdido la celebración de Japón si hubiera ganado una competición que se le resiste desde hace 28 años. Los estadounidenses remontaron y se llevaron el triunfo por 17-13. En cambio, su precipitada salida encontró recompensa en Japón. El número 32 del mundo se llevó la victoria con 262 golpes y 18 bajo par tras una gran última vuelta de 64 (-6) para imponerse con tres golpes de ventaja sobre el japonés Kazuki Higa, que terminó con -15. El golfista surcoreano, con 13 triunfos profesionales, cuatro de ellos en el PGA Tour, se libra de este modo de los casi dos años de servicio militar obligatorio que deben cumplir todos los hombres, salvo contadas excepciones. El período de tiempo al servicio del ejército va de 18 a 21 meses. Las exenciones especiales quedan limitadas a artistas o deportistas que destacan en competiciones internacionales vinculadas al prestigio nacional. En el caso de los deportistas surcoreanos, una medalla en los Juegos Olímpicos (Kim rozó el bronce en París 2024 al acabar a cuatro golpes del tercer puesto), pero se quedó o un oro individual o por equipos en los Juegos Asiáticos permite no realizar la mili. Kim sí deberá completar la formación militar básica y quedará encuadrado como personal deportivo durante 34 meses. Durante ese periodo deberá completar 544 horas de servicio comunitario relacionado con el deporte.

articles.title: Falcons Honeymooners Face Tough Test In New Orleans Dome
articles.summary: Falcons honeymooners head to New Orleans for the Domecoming. Can Atlanta handle the noise and the history? The stats say it will be brutal.
articles.body:
Two Falcons fans are spending their honeymoon in New Orleans this week. They picked the one game in Atlanta's schedule that matters most to the city. This isn't just a date. It is a trip to the Superdome for the 20th anniversary of the Saints' return after Hurricane Katrina. The atmosphere will be thick with history and hate for the visiting team. While the couple celebrates, the Falcons must survive a hostile crowd that has not forgotten 20 years of rivalry.

New Orleans is not a normal road game. The Superdome creates a pressure cooker that breaks visiting teams. Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski knows this reality better than anyone. He told reporters that "In this league, you go on the road; you get to experience some incredible crowds." That sounds polite. The truth is much darker for Atlanta. The Saints are 1-2, but they have played close games. The Falcons are also 1-2, yet they have been erratic. One week they get crushed 34-3 to Carolina, the next they beat the Packers. That inconsistency is a death sentence in a place like this.

Old rivals want to turn the Falcons into "Trashlanta." Long-time Saints defensive end Cameron Jordan said, "You know the importance of this game," before adding, "'Can'tlanta' comes to the dome. We have to turn them into 'Trashlanta.'" That is not a friendly jab. It is a promise of pain. The Falcons have to deal with the emotional weight of a city that feels like a family reunion gone wrong.

Quarterback Michael Penix Jr. has one job: keep his head up. He handled the Green Bay crowd well in his last start. Stefanski praised him, noting, "Mike did an outstanding job both in the huddle and at the line of scrimmage the other night, and getting us in and out of the correct plays, making adjustments when necessary." The stats back this up. Penix threw for 256 yards. Bijan Robinson ran for 194 yards and two touchdowns. Drake London caught nine passes for 194 yards. These are huge numbers. But numbers from Green Bay mean nothing in New Orleans.

The Saints have a run defense that ranks 27th in the league. They are weak against the run. Yet the Falcons are 29th in pass defense themselves. This is a trap. The Saints will throw deep with Tyler Shough and Chris Olave. They are third in the NFL in passing offense. If Penix slips up, the crowd will eat him alive. The Falcons need to lean on their best unit. They are second in rushing and have the best run defense in the league. They gave up just 47.7 yards per game. They held the Packers to 17 rushing yards. That is the only way to win.

New Orleans is not invincible. They lost their home opener to Las Vegas 35-27. They squandered an 11-point lead and turned the ball over four times. Tight end Juwan Johnson tried to calm fans, saying, "We've only played three games. It's nothing to panic over." He claimed the team is "playing really aggressive, really strong, really physical, really smart and really fast." But mistakes cost them. All three are 1-2, but Carolina currently holds the division lead on tiebreakers. Every game is a must-win.

The Saints also lost their top rusher, Travis Etienne Jr., to a hamstring injury. He is out for at least four weeks. They will rely on Alvin Kamara and Kendre Miller. Coach Kellen Moore said, "We feel fortunate that we have Alvin." But the offense still needs to protect the ball. The Falcons have the tools to exploit a messy Saints team. The question is if they can handle the noise. The couple on their honeymoon will see a packed house. The Falcons will see a wall of sound. They must block it out.

articles.title: How Tony Romo got on while playing PGA Tour Q-School event
articles.summary: Tony Romo is still trying to crack the world of professional golf. The former Dallas Cowboys quarterback is an exceptional golfer.
articles.body:
Tony Romo is still trying to crack the world of professional golf. The former Dallas Cowboys quarterback is an exceptional golfer. His handicap is around +3, and he regularly dominates high-profile celebrity events, winning the American Century Championship multiple times.

However, when he tests his game against professional fields through sponsor exemptions on the PGA Tour and Korn Ferry Tour, the gap between elite amateurs and touring professionals becomes apparent.

He shot a 77 in his PGA Tour debut and has consistently missed the cut in professional tournaments. Under the bright lights of the PGA Tour, even minor holes in your game get exposed.

He recently went through pre-qualifying at Q-School in Oklahoma, and once again it didn't quite go to plan.

How Tony Romo performed in Q-School pre-qualifying event

Romo's pre-qualifying event in Oklahoma looked promising for a while. The 46-year-old was in contention to make it into the top 37 and advance through the pre-qualifying stage. He was T46 with nine holes to play after a birdie on the ninth.

However, it all came undone. Romo shot a 74 in his third and final round to finish nine-over par, four shots above the cutline as play concluded. It was a disappointing end to what could have been a huge success for Romo.

Romo has competed in PGA Tour Q-School pre-qualifying five times and has played in several PGA Tour tournaments with a sponsor's exemption. He's also tried to qualify for the US Open several times to no avail.

But to make matters worse, while he was competing in Oklahoma, CBS announced it was parting ways with Romo, who previously commentated on their NFL coverage. Romo was arrested in late July for a DUI while leaving the Wisconsin Amateur Golf Championship.

CBS initially placed Romo on leave for the start of the NFL season, but has now made the move permanent by officially cutting ties with the former Cowboys star.

They said in a statement: "CBS Sports and Tony Romo have mutually agreed to part ways. We thank Tony for his contributions over the past nine years and wish him the best moving forward."

So it didn't go his way on the course, and CBS let him go off the course. A poor day all round for Romo.
